signals.topic: Team cancel_run does not cascade to member agents — wastes tokens and compute
signals.summary: When cancel_run(team_run_id) is called, only team-level execution stops. Member agents continue to completion because each generates its own run_id via uuid4(), so raise_if_cancelled() inside member agents never detects the parent's cancelled_runs entry. This causes unbounded token, time, and compute waste on runs the user explicitly intended to stop.
aliases: team cancel not propagating to members
member agent runs continue after team cancellation
signals.review_reason: count=1 但提供了完整复现代码，用户影响明确：用户主动取消团队运行但子 agent 仍消耗 token 和算力完成执行，直接造成经济损失，属于主流程阻断行为（P1）。

source_issues.title: Team cancel does not cascade to currently-running member agents
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction script provided showing slow agent completing after team.cancel_run(); causes wasted tokens/compute on user-cancelled runs

signals.topic: SSL certificate verification not configurable in MCPTools — blocks enterprise self-signed cert connections
signals.summary: MCPTools and MultiMCPTools have no ssl_verify or cert_path parameters. When connecting to MCP servers over HTTPS that use self-signed certificates or internal CAs (common in enterprise environments), the connection silently fails. Users have no workaround other than manually editing system CA store files.
signals.review_reason: 企业用户无法连接使用自签名证书或内部 CA 的 MCP 服务器，直接阻断集成场景。虽然标注为 enhancement，但用户影响证据具体（阻断连接），定 P1。

source_issues.title: Support for SSL Verification and Custom Cert Paths in MCP Tools

signals.topic: AgentOS API exposes system prompts, model config, and tool call results to all clients with no filter
signals.summary: AgentResponse.from_agent() unconditionally includes system_message.instructions (confidential prompts), model config, tools list, and tool execution results in API responses. SSE streams emit full ToolCallStarted/ToolCallCompleted events with raw tool inputs/outputs with no built-in suppression mechanism. This is a production security gap for deployments where the API is accessible to untrusted frontends or end users.
signals.review_reason: 有明确用户影响证据：生产部署中系统提示词（含机密业务逻辑）、工具配置和工具调用 I/O 无条件暴露给 API 客户端，无过滤机制。虽然标注 enhancement 但本质是安全信息泄露问题，威胁企业级生产部署安全，P1。

source_issues.title: AgentOS exposes sensitive agent internals to API clients — system prompt, model config, tools, and tool call results
source_issues.evidence: Production deployments with accessible API leak full system prompts, tool names/configs, and raw tool call I/O to any client with no opt-out mechanism

signals.topic: PIIDetectionGuardrail custom_patterns crashes with AttributeError on raw regex strings

The code requires compiled patterns (re.compile(...)) but this is undocumented, leading to silent failure or a crash when users follow the natural API usage pattern.
signals.review_reason: PII 防护栏是安全关键组件，传入 raw regex 字符串会导致 AttributeError 崩溃。文档也未说明需要 re.compile()，属于 API 使用体验陷阱和意外崩溃（P2）。

signals.topic: Select-All (Ctrl-A/Cmd-A) no longer selects text in input field — regression across multiple OS and terminal combinations
signals.summary: Ctrl-A/Cmd-A in the input field no longer selects all text; instead it visually highlights large portions of the screen. Affects macOS, Ubuntu, Debian across multiple terminal emulators (Ghostty, iTerm2, Proxmox noVNC). Regressed since v1.2.x through v1.14.33. This is a core text interaction regression that disrupts daily workflow for all users on affected platforms.

Severity is high despite count=1 due to breadth of impact (OS+terminal combinations) and absence of workarounds.

source_issues.title: cmd-A or control-A does not select all in the input field anymore

signals.topic: Electron desktop app stalls 5-10s during burst of storage writes (session/project switching)
signals.summary: Electron main process serializes every renderer store-set IPC call to immediate electron-store writes. During session/project switching with many persisted UI-state updates (100+ writes, ~40-50ms each), the main process stalls for 5-10 seconds. Users cannot switch sessions or projects smoothly. Storage-layer coalescer fix identified but not yet upstreamed.
aliases: desktop app freezes on session switch
signals.review_reason: Electron desktop core functionality is blocked — session and project switching become unresponsive for 5-10 seconds. This is a main-process architecture issue that blocks common daily operations. Multiple related prior issues cited (#16256, #16251, #11329, #11328, #20977, #24227, #19082), indicating a known systemic problem. Count=1 here reflects this single report, but severity and user impact meet P0 threshold.

source_issues.title: Electron desktop stalls during bursts of storage writes
source_issues.evidence: Traces show 100+ writes to opencode.global.dat during session/project switching, each ~40-50ms, causing 5-10s stalls. Reproducible on macOS Apple Silicon Electron desktop. Working fix (storage-layer coalescer) implemented in a fork but not yet upstreamed.

signals.topic: Custom-baseURL OpenAI provider authentication hijacked by residual OAuth credential — users locked out of API-key mode
signals.summary: Users who have ever logged in via ChatGPT OAuth cannot use API-key mode for any custom-baseURL OpenAI provider. OpenCode always injects the OAuth JWT regardless of config apiKey. Three attempted workarounds all fail: (1) keep oauth in auth.json — JWT forwarded upstream causing deactivated_workspace errors; (2) switch to api key type in config — Authorization header empty, proxy requires auth; (3) delete openai entry — TypeError crash on subagent call. Net effect: locked out of self-hosted/OpenRouter/LiteLLM proxy with OpenAI provider.
aliases: oauth credential conflicts with api-key mode
ChatGPT OAuth breaks OpenAI API key config
signals.review_reason: This is a complete auth path failure: users who have ever used ChatGPT OAuth are permanently locked out of using any OpenAI-compatible proxy (OpenRouter, LiteLLM, self-hosted) with the openai provider. Three independent workarounds all fail, leaving no viable path. This is a primary use-case blocker.

source_issues.title: Custom-baseURL openai provider is hijacked by residual oauth credential in auth.json
source_issues.evidence: Three distinct failure modes confirmed, all reproducible. OAuth JWT forwarded upstream by proxy causing deactivated_workspace errors. apiKey field never maps to @ai-sdk/openai options.apiKey. Deleting openai entry causes TypeError: undefined is not an object at fetch. Issue closed by maintainer with no resolution path visible to user.

signals.topic: Highlight-copy of code blocks drops empty lines — copied code structurally incorrect
signals.summary: When users click to copy code emitted by OpenCode agents, the highlight-copy mechanism does not preserve empty lines within code blocks. Pasted code is structurally different from the original (missing blank lines), causing potential bugs when the code is used. Affects all users on all platforms.
signals.review_reason: Code output copied by users is structurally incorrect — missing empty lines can change code semantics (e.g., in Python/JS blank lines affect readability and in some cases behavior). This is a data integrity issue in a core workflow (copying agent-generated code) affecting all users.

source_issues.title: Highlight-copy code doesn't preserve empty lines
source_issues.evidence: Screenshot comparison shows generated code on left vs pasted code on right — empty lines are missing in the pasted version. Structural correctness of code is compromised. Reproduced on macOS 15.7.5 + Ghostty 1.2.3.

signals.topic: Plugin provider.models() hook regression — custom/self-hosted providers can no longer register models dynamically
signals.summary: After PR #25167 (merged April 30 2026, shipped in v1.14.x), the plugin provider.models() hook skips all custom providers not present in the models.dev catalog. Custom providers (local proxies, self-hosted endpoints, corporate gateways) declared in opencode.jsonc cannot be populated with dynamic model discovery. The hook now looks up the models.dev database instead of the live providers map, short-circuiting for any non-catalog provider. Users must hardcode every model manually.
aliases: plugin model hook skips custom providers
self-hosted LLM provider models not populating
signals.review_reason: Plugin ecosystem regression: any plugin that augments custom/non-catalog providers with dynamically discovered models is now broken. This affects a core extensibility mechanism and forces users to manually maintain model lists. Count=1 but root cause is a specific regression PR with clear evidence. Impact is significant for self-hosted/local LLM users.

source_issues.title: Regression: plugin provider.models() hook no longer populates custom providers (post #25167)
source_issues.evidence: Root cause precisely identified: PR #25167 moved plugin hook iteration to run before configProviders merge and changed lookup from live providers map to database (models.dev catalog). Custom provider IDs not in database are skipped. Full reproduction steps with working vs broken code comparison provided.

signals.topic: Bedrock streaming error SSE events cause AttributeError crashes in production
signals.summary: When Bedrock cross-region inference returns HTTP 200 with an error-type SSE frame (e.g., rate_limit_error), the SDK decodes it into a BetaRawMessageStartEvent whose `message` field is None. Any downstream code accessing `event.message.model` or `event.message.usage` immediately raises AttributeError, crashing the application. Affects production use of AsyncAnthropicBedrock with `global.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7`.
signals.review_reason: Production crash causing AttributeError in active streaming loops. The SDK produces a None-valued message object that crashes user code on any attribute access. This is a runtime exception that blocks the streaming workflow end-to-end.

source_issues.title: Streaming error SSE event causes `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute` errors
source_issues.evidence: Production crash with full stack trace: `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'model'` and `'usage'`. Bedrock returns HTTP 200 + error SSE frame `{'type': 'error', 'error': {'type': 'rate_limit_error'}}` which the SDK decodes into a BetaRawMessageStartEvent with `message=None`. Any access to `event.message.<anything>` raises AttributeError. Reproducible with minimal repro script looping 200 requests.

signals.topic: Bedrock streaming SSE error events raise bare ValueError instead of user-facing APIStatusError
signals.summary: When Bedrock SSE streams return non-200 HTTP status in the SSE payload (e.g., status_code=400 with internalServerException), the SDK raises an unhandled bare ValueError instead of surfacing it as an APIStatusError. Users cannot catch or handle the error gracefully, and the wrong exception type masks the actual API error.
aliases: bedrock streaming valueerror bad response code
signals.review_reason: Users cannot catch or handle Bedrock streaming errors because the SDK raises ValueError instead of the user-facing APIStatusError. This prevents graceful error recovery and masks the actual API error details from the user.

source_issues.title: Bedrock streaming SSE events errors are not handled gracefully
source_issues.evidence: Full stack trace shows `ValueError: Bad response code, expected 200` raised from `anthropic/lib/bedrock/_stream_decoder.py` line 58. Bedrock SSE stream returns `{'status_code': 400, ':exception-type': 'internalServerException'}`. The ValueError is unhandled and not converted to APIStatusError, preventing users from catching and handling it.

signals.topic: AsyncAnthropicVertex sends requests to wrong endpoint for US/EU regions causing 404 errors
signals.summary: AsyncAnthropicVertex constructs incorrect API endpoints when region is set to 'us' or 'eu', sending requests to `us-aiplatform.googleapis.com` instead of `aiplatform.us.rep.googleapis.com`. The same code works correctly with the synchronous AnthropicVertex client. Users are blocked from using async Vertex AI in US and EU regions.
aliases: vertex ai async region endpoint mismatch
signals.review_reason: Async client is completely broken for US and EU regions due to wrong endpoint construction, returning 404. The sync client works fine for the same inputs, clearly indicating a regression or bug in the async code path. Users are blocked from using the async client in those regions.

source_issues.title: Async methods NOT working with US/EU regions on Vertex AI - Gets 404 on endpoints
source_issues.evidence: AsyncAnthropicVertex sends POST to `https://us-aiplatform.googleapis.com/...` (404) while synchronous AnthropicVertex sends to `https://aiplatform.us.rep.googleapis.com/...` (200). Region 'global' works for both. User blocked from async Vertex AI in US/EU regions.

signals.topic: Streaming /v1/messages drops mid-stream with RemoteProtocolError on long code_execution + skills runs, causing cost loss on retries
signals.summary: Streaming requests using beta messages API with code_execution and skills betas consistently drop mid-stream with `httpx.RemoteProtocolError: peer closed connection without sending complete message body`. The server closes the connection while content_block_delta events are actively being sent, not due to idle timeout. Each retry re-bills for the full input tokens plus previously-generated partial output tokens, causing direct monetary cost loss.
aliases: streaming connection closed during code execution
signals.review_reason: Production mid-stream connection drops that directly cause monetary loss through re-billing on each retry. Author explicitly describes 'Each retry costs full input + previously-billed partial output tokens.' This is a cost-loss pain point, not merely a UX nuisance. Also has cross-SDK evidence (TypeScript SDK same issue, #842). P0 despite count=1 due to direct financial impact and cross-SDK evidence.

source_issues.title: Streaming /v1/messages drops mid-stream with RemoteProtocolError on long code_execution + skills runs
source_issues.evidence: Full incident: 38 content blocks streamed (6 text, 16 server_tool_use, 16 tool_result) then stream died mid-text_editor_code_execution.input_json_delta. Server actively sending bytes when FIN arrived. Network error triggers retry with full input re-submission + partial output re-billing. Author explicitly states each retry costs full input + previously-billed partial output tokens. Same symptom reported in anthropic-sdk-typescript#842 (open, unacknowledged).

signals.topic: Skills Files API creates untracked orphan files that accumulate indefinitely with no safe garbage-collection mechanism
signals.summary: When users create skills with attached files via beta.skills.create(files=[...]), those files accumulate on the account with no exposed linkage back to the skill that owns them. beta.skills.versions.retrieve does not return the file_ids, and beta.files.list does not expose skill_id or scope. Deleting a skill does not cascade-delete its backing files, and there is no filter on files.list to identify which files are skill-owned. In production, this causes indefinite file accumulation (1100+ files) with no safe deletion path.
signals.review_reason: Data hygiene/cost issue causing indefinite accumulation of untrackable files. User has 1100+ files with no safe deletion path — blind delete-all breaks live skills. This is a direct storage cost and account management pain point. The issue also compounds over time as each skill re-provisioning adds more orphans.

source_issues.title: Cannot GC orphan Files API files — skill→file linkage not exposed on skills.versions.retrieve
source_issues.evidence: User has ~1100 files on a single account with no way to distinguish 'referenced vs orphan'. beta.skills.versions.retrieve response lacks any `files` field. beta.files.list returns files with `scope: None` and no back-reference. Deleting a skill leaves its backing files orphaned. User calls out 'We can't safely delete files without knowing which skills reference them.' Each provisioning cycle accumulates more orphan files.

signals.topic: Build breaks after v0.91.1 due to broken @ts-ignore formatting in dist files causing TS2307 compilation errors
signals.summary: Since v0.91.1, stainless-app started formatting dist/* files, breaking @ts-ignore comment syntax from `/* @ts-ignore ... */` to `// @ts-ignore ... */`, which causes TypeScript compilation errors (TS2307: Cannot find module) for end users.
signals.review_reason: 虽然 count=1 不是高频，但这是 v0.91.1 发布引入的回归问题，导致用户 build 失败阻断，属于主流程阻断问题。且是最近3天内关闭的活跃 issue，有明确 TS 编译错误证据，应保留为 P1 而非 P2。

source_issues.title: Bug: Broken dist `@ts-ignore` in v0.91.1
source_issues.evidence: TypeScript compilation fails with TS2307 error in internal/types.d.ts due to broken @ts-ignore syntax. User reports their build is broken after upgrading to v0.91.1.

signals.topic: AWS Bedrock SDK streaming drops error information (status code) making retry logic impossible
signals.summary: The AWS Bedrock SDK's SSE stream parsing silently drops error details including HTTP status codes, preventing users from implementing proper retry logic for failed streams.
signals.review_reason: Bedrock SDK 流式处理时丢失错误信息，用户无法判断何时应该重试，直接影响生产环境错误恢复能力。虽然 count=1，但有截图证据且问题存在于长时间活跃的 issue 中，属于明显的 workflow runtime 问题，用户影响具体（无法实现 retry），应保留为 P1。

source_issues.title: AWS Bedrock SDK: Error information is lost when streaming
source_issues.evidence: Error information (status code) is lost when parsing SSE streams in Bedrock SDK. User demonstrates that errors are difficult to parse for retry decisions. Issue has been recently re-activated, indicating ongoing user pain.

signals.topic: MCP server tools fail to register on Windows; agent receives 'No such tool available' for all MCP tools
signals.summary: On Windows, when the SDK spawns a worker with an MCP server via stdio transport, the server's instructions are injected into the agent's context but all tools return 'No such tool available'. The agentic workflow is completely blocked — the agent cannot perform any work using MCP tools. The same code worked on 2026-04-30 and began failing 100% reproducibly afterward with no code changes.
aliases: MCP tools not callable on Windows
stdio MCP injection fails silently on Windows
signals.review_reason: Main flow is completely blocked for Windows users relying on MCP servers. The agent cannot perform any meaningful work — tools are injected into context but are not callable. This is a regression from a previously working state (2026-04-30). Affects production agentic workflows. Excluded from P0 only because count=1 and single repo.

source_issues.title: MCP server tools fail to register on Windows: server config visible to agent but tools return 'No such tool available'
source_issues.evidence: Agent reports MCP server's instructions are visible but tools are not callable. Every call to MCP tools returns 'No such tool available'. 100% reproducible across ~6 attempts. Blocks all agentic workflows that depend on stdio MCP servers.

signals.topic: Subprocess CLI crashes with AttributeError when system_prompt is passed as list of content blocks (Anthropic API-supported format)
signals.summary: When a caller passes system_prompt as a list of content blocks (which is valid per Anthropic Messages API and recommended for prompt caching with cache_control on individual blocks), the SubprocessCLITransport._build_command method crashes with AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get'. The crash occurs at command-build time before any model call, burning API costs ($0.46 reported in one instance) with zero output.
aliases: system_prompt content blocks not supported by CLI transport
signals.review_reason: Main flow crashes immediately with a traceback when users pass the Anthropic-recommended list-form system_prompt. Prevents use of prompt caching with per-block cache_control. Explicit monetary cost reported ($0.46 per failed run). Workaround requires abandoning the recommended caching pattern. This is a direct API compatibility gap between SDK and upstream Anthropic API.

source_issues.title: subprocess CLI rejects list-form system_prompt (Anthropic API supports it)
source_issues.evidence: Crash occurs at SubprocessCLITransport._build_command before any API call. Reported monetary cost: $0.46 burned in a single failed invocation. Users cannot use prompt caching with per-block cache_control, which is the Anthropic-recommended pattern. Workaround requires collapsing to a concatenated string, losing layer-independent caching benefits.

signals.topic: ProcessError exit_code and stderr stripped during error propagation; users catch generic Exception and see hard-coded placeholder
signals.summary: When the bundled CLI subprocess exits non-zero, the original ProcessError (with structured exit_code and stderr fields) is destroyed during propagation. Users catch a bare Exception, cannot access exit_code, and the stderr field shows only the hard-coded literal 'Check stderr output for details' — never the actual subprocess output. Multiple closed issues (#515, #282, #238) are variants of the same problem.
aliases: ProcessError type destroyed on subprocess failure
stderr not captured in ProcessError propagation
Generic Exception raised instead of ProcessError
exit_code not accessible from caught exception
signals.review_reason: Subprocess failure diagnosis is made impossible by this bug — users cannot programmatically access exit_code or stderr, making it impossible to write proper error handlers or distinguish between different subprocess failure modes. This is a recurring pain point with at least 3 prior closed issues on the same theme. Blocks proper error handling in production and CI environments.

source_issues.title: ProcessError exit_code/stderr stripped during error propagation; users see generic Exception with hard-coded 'Check stderr output for details' placeholder
source_issues.evidence: Verified reproduction shows isinstance(exc, ProcessError) is False when subprocess fails, exc.stderr is absent, exc.exit_code is absent. Three compounding defects across three files destroy all structured error information. Closed issues #515, #282, #238 are referenced as variants. In concurrent/CI setups, users have no programmatic way to associate stderr with a specific failed call.

signals.topic: API 400 errors with no body cause complete workflow blockage and lack retryability
signals.summary: API returns 400 status code with no response body, making it impossible for users to understand why requests fail. The error is marked canRetry=false, so users cannot automatically recover. Appears 8+ times across multiple sessions, completely blocking the conversation flow.
signals.review_reason: This is a primary workflow blocker: API 400 errors with no body appear 8 times across 4 events in a 1.5-hour window, each completely blocking user conversation. The canRetry=false flag prevents automatic recovery, forcing manual intervention. The error message provides zero diagnostic detail, making root cause investigation impossible for affected users.

source_issues.title: 400 status code (no body)
source_issues.evidence: 8 occurrences in 1.5 hours across 4 independent events. Error message: '400 status code (no body) — Endpoint rejected the request with no body (no obvious shape problem). canRetry: false.' Completely blocks user conversation with no diagnostic detail.

signals.topic: SDK causes excessive cache_creation_input_tokens on every turn leading to significant cost overrun
signals.summary: The SDK marks ~65K tokens as cache_creation_input_tokens per turn even on null-content exchanges, instead of reusing cached content. This causes a ~$5K/month cost overrun for fleet users who expect near-zero cache creation costs on trivial turns.
aliases: cache write cost leak per turn
unnecessary ephemeral cache writes causing cost inflation
signals.review_reason: This is a direct cost loss issue: the SDK forces ~65K cache_creation_input_tokens per turn regardless of content, costing ~$5K/month for a 35-agent fleet. The cache_read mechanism works correctly, proving the content is already cached — yet the SDK pays the write cost every turn. This is a clear, quantifiable financial impact per the user's detailed telemetry data.

source_issues.title: cache issues in sdk
source_issues.evidence: Per-turn cost on Opus is $0.50-$0.65 even for trivial null-content exchanges, dominated by ~65K cache_create tokens. At 50 turns/day across 35 fleet agents = ~$175/day fleet-wide = ~$5K/month attributable to this floor. Content already cached and being read correctly (cache_read working), yet SDK pays 1.25x cache-write rate instead of 0.1x cache-read rate.

signals.topic: sandbox.network.allowedDomains configuration is silently ignored for Bash tool and WebFetch
signals.summary: The sandbox network domain allowlist configuration is accepted by the SDK but has zero enforcement. Bash subprocesses and WebFetch requests bypass all restrictions, creating a false sense of security for users relying on network isolation.
signals.review_reason: This is a security/isolation regression: the SDK accepts a network allowlist configuration but has zero enforcement mechanism at the OS level. Bash and WebFetch both bypass restrictions silently. Users relying on sandbox network isolation for security or compliance purposes are unknowingly unprotected. The gap is documented by the user with clear root cause analysis.

source_issues.title: `sandbox.network.allowedDomains` not enforced for Bash tool or WebFetch
source_issues.evidence: SDK accepts sandbox.network.allowedDomains config but Bash subprocesses make unrestricted network calls and WebFetch requests are not blocked. Root cause: no OS-level enforcement (no proxy, no pf rules, no seccomp/bubblewrap, no Darwin Sandbox). Users who configure network restrictions get silent bypass.

signals.topic: OTel spans use Anthropic-native token attribute names instead of OTel GenAI semantic convention, breaking observability tooling
signals.summary: The SDK emits token counts as Anthropic-native names (input_tokens, output_tokens) on OTel spans, but OTel GenAI convention-aware backends expect gen_ai.usage.input_tokens. This causes all token counts to appear as zero in downstream observability tools, making per-LLM-call cost attribution impossible.
aliases: GenAI semantic convention not followed for usage metrics
OTel span token attributes not OTel-compliant
signals.review_reason: This is an observability breakdown: token counts on OTel spans appear as zero in any GenAI-convention-aware backend due to attribute name mismatch. Per-call cost attribution from traces alone becomes impossible, forcing consumers to bypass OTel or compute costs locally. While the issue is closed, it represents a real usability gap for users relying on standard OTel tooling for LLM cost monitoring.

source_issues.title: OTel telemetry: token counts emitted as input_tokens/output_tokens instead of OTel GenAI semantic convention gen_ai.usage.*
source_issues.evidence: SDK emits Anthropic-native attribute names (input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_creation_tokens) on claude_code.llm_request spans. OTel GenAI-convention-aware parsers see total_tokens: 0, prompt_tokens: 0, completion_tokens: 0, total_cost: 0 — all zeroes despite nonzero API responses. Per-LLM-call cost attribution from traces alone is impossible without special-case workarounds.

signals.topic: GitHub App auth fails without uninstall events, blocking PR review workflows
signals.summary: Previously-working GitHub Actions across multiple repos in an organization started failing with 'Claude Code is not installed' error, despite no uninstall events in the audit log. Requiring manual reinstall of the Claude App restores functionality. This blocks the main PR review workflow entirely.
aliases: GitHub App uninstall without audit evidence
signals.review_reason: Main PR review workflow completely blocked across an entire organization. Despite being count=1, the issue describes a real production outage affecting multiple repos at once, with clear user impact (workflows fail, require manual reinstall). The audit log anomaly (no uninstall events but app appears uninstalled) suggests a service-side issue that could affect any user at any time.

source_issues.title: [BUG] "Claude Code is not installed on this repository" for previously-working github actions across multiple repos on 2026-04-28
source_issues.evidence: Main review workflow failed across multiple repos simultaneously on 2026-04-28. Audit log shows no uninstall events. Manual reinstall of Claude App was required to restore functionality. State: closed (resolved by manual reinstall).

signals.topic: False positive multi-operation detection blocks valid bash commands (awk &&, python3 -c, Windows path)
signals.summary: The safety detector incorrectly flags valid bash commands as multi-operation or suspicious, blocking them and accumulating approval prompts until all 80 turns are exhausted, causing job cancellation.
signals.review_reason: Valid, common bash commands are incorrectly blocked, causing the job to exhaust all available turns and be cancelled. This is a direct workflow failure — users cannot complete PR review tasks using standard Unix commands. The detection logic has at least 3 distinct false positive patterns affecting common use cases.

source_issues.title: False positive multi-operation detection blocks valid bash commands (awk, python3 -c, Windows path pattern)
source_issues.evidence: Three distinct false positive patterns observed: (1) awk with && inside pattern is blocked as command chaining, (2) python3 -c inline script blocked as multiple operations, (3) file path ending in '0:' flagged as Windows drive letter. All accumulate approval prompts until 80-turn limit is exhausted and job is cancelled.

signals.topic: .claude-pr/ snapshot directory accidentally committed to user PR branch by bot fix-up commits
signals.summary: When the Claude bot makes fix-up commits in PR context, the .claude-pr/ snapshot directory created by restoreConfigFromBase is inadvertently included in the commit, polluting the PR with unrelated files. The bot's reply comment does not acknowledge this stealth commit.
signals.review_reason: PR history is polluted with unrelated files committed by the bot without any user notification. This creates confusion during code review, requires users to manually clean up the git history, and repeats on every subsequent @claude invocation. The bot's silent acknowledgment makes this particularly insidious.

source_issues.title: `restoreConfigFromBase` snapshot at `.claude-pr/` gets committed to PR branch when bot pushes a fix
source_issues.evidence: Two real-world stealth commits in a private org repo: initial .claude-pr/ snapshot (~100 files) committed on unrelated PR, and a re-sync commit on another PR. Bot reply summarizes only the requested fix with no mention of the extra commit. Repeated on subsequent @claude runs.

signals.topic: restoreConfigFromBase misses nested CLAUDE.md files, creating prompt injection surface
signals.summary: restoreConfigFromBase restores root-level CLAUDE.md files from the base branch but not nested CLAUDE.md files, leaving a prompt injection surface where PR-modified instruction files at any directory depth can shape Claude's behavior.
signals.review_reason: Security/consistency gap: the fix for root CLAUDE.md prompt injection (#1174) was not applied to nested CLAUDE.md files, creating an inconsistent security boundary. While no active exploitation is reported, this is a known attack surface with a clear precedent fix. Keeping as P2 because it is non-blocking (no confirmed exploitation) but represents a real security design flaw.

source_issues.title: `restoreConfigFromBase` should cover nested `CLAUDE.md` files
source_issues.evidence: Claude Code auto-loads nested CLAUDE.md from any directory depth, but restoreConfigFromBase only covers root-level entries. A nested CLAUDE.md modified in a PR will remain on disk and be loaded by Claude Code, bypassing the base-branch restore protection that was added for root CLAUDE.md.

signals.topic: trigger_phrase matching is case-sensitive, silently failing on mobile iOS autocorrect
signals.summary: The trigger phrase matching uses case-sensitive regex, so @claude does not match @Claude or @CLAUDE. On iOS, autocorrect capitalizes @claude to @Claude, causing the action to silently skip the trigger with no user-visible error, even though GitHub's workflow-level contains() guard passes.
signals.review_reason: Users on mobile iOS get a silent failure — the workflow runs but the action does nothing. This is a degraded experience with no error signal to the user about why the action was skipped. The fix is trivial (add 'i' flag to regex) but the impact on mobile users is real and consistent.

source_issues.title: trigger_phrase matching is case-sensitive, should be case-insensitive
source_issues.evidence: On mobile iOS, @claude gets autocorrected to @Claude. The workflow runs (GitHub contains() is case-insensitive) but the action silently skips the trigger. User sees 'No trigger found' with no explanation. State: closed (suggested fix provided).

signals.topic: Rate limit / quota exhaustion early in session despite paid credits purchase
signals.summary: Users hitting 429 rate limit errors early in a session despite recently purchasing credits. One user purchased $1,000 in credits and still received 'You've hit your limit'. Another user in early session stage with full quota experienced the same. Suggests incorrect quota tracking or billing system integration failure.
signals.review_reason: Two separate users experiencing premature quota exhaustion with explicit financial loss evidence. The combination of early-session exhaustion after credit purchase and the explicit refund request indicates a perceived billing/quota tracking failure that causes users to lose access to a paid product before their purchased credits should be exhausted.

source_issues.title: You've hit your limit · resets May 5 at 9pm (America/New_York)
source_issues.evidence: User purchased $1,000 in credits, still hitting 429 rate_limit_error on first session usage. Direct financial loss evidence.

source_issues.title: You're out of extra usage · resets 9:50pm (America/Sao_Paulo)
source_issues.evidence: Rate limit hit on early stage of task with full quota at start. User explicitly states 'no way to be exceeding quota window so fast, please reset and refund'. Explicit perceived billing system failure.

signals.topic: VS Code Remote-SSH: 'Open in New Tab' command throws blocking error dialog on every use
signals.summary: Running Claude Code: Open in New Tab from the command palette via VS Code Remote-SSH causes an error dialog every time: command 'workbench.action.moveEditorToEndOfGroup' not found. The dialog blocks until dismissed. Only affects server-side extension install in Remote-SSH, not local installs.
signals.review_reason: Blocking error dialog that interrupts workflow on every use of a core VS Code extension command. While the panel eventually opens, the repeated dismissable error dialog is a recurring experience that degrades the Remote-SSH extension quality.

source_issues.title: "Open in New Tab" pops error: command 'workbench.action.moveEditorToEndOfGroup' not found
source_issues.evidence: Error dialog blocks user until dismissed on every use of Open in New Tab in Remote-SSH. Has explicit reproduction steps and confirmed 100% reproducible.

signals.topic: CLI --output-format json emits invalid JSON when model output contains unescaped quotes
signals.summary: When using --output-format json, the result field in the JSON envelope can contain a bare ASCII double-quote inside a string value without proper escaping, making the entire output unparseable as JSON and breaking all programmatic consumers.
signals.review_reason: CLI --output-format json is a core integration point for automation pipelines. When it emits invalid JSON, all downstream consumers fail silently or crash. This is a data integrity failure in the primary machine-readable output format.

source_issues.title: [BUG] --output-format json result field contains invalid JSON when model uses unescaped " in string values
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible with claude -p --output-format json using German quotation marks. Result field contains unescaped U+0022 inside JSON string, breaking downstream json.Unmarshal for any automation consuming the output.

signals.topic: /review command broken by GitHub Projects Classic GraphQL API deprecation
signals.summary: Running /review on a PR causes gh pr view to fail with a GraphQL error: Projects (classic) is being deprecated. The error cancels the parallel gh pr diff call, making /review completely unusable for users with GitHub Projects Classic configured.
signals.review_reason: A core /review skill is entirely broken for users who have GitHub Projects Classic configured on their repositories. The GraphQL field is officially deprecated by GitHub as of 2024, meaning this is a sustained, widening impact as more repositories migrate.

source_issues.title: [BUG] /review deprecation issue:
source_issues.evidence: /review command fails with exit code 1 on gh pr view due to GitHub Projects Classic GraphQL field deprecation. Parallel tool call to gh pr diff is cancelled as a result, making the entire /review command unusable.

signals.topic: Cowork FUSE cache (1-hour TTL) causes silent file truncation and data corruption
signals.summary: Cowork's rclone FUSE mount uses a 3600-second cache for the outputs/user-data mount. After using Edit/Write tools, bash reads stale cached content for up to 1 hour. This causes silent file truncation, missing functions, and lost code with no error or warning. Claude proceeds confidently on stale data. Documented impact: 8 files corrupted in a single project including portal/index.html truncated from 791 to 648 lines, App.js showing 6 lines instead of 59. Estimated 3-4 hours of user time wasted per session.
signals.review_reason: Silent data corruption in Cowork is P0: there is no error or warning, Claude proceeds confidently on stale data, and the impact includes lost code across multiple files per session. The 3600-second cache is server-side and unfixable by users. The uploads mount proves a 1-second cache works for the same infrastructure, indicating a fixable configuration issue. Evidence includes server-side mount inspection and a per-file impact table.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Cowork: Stale rclone FUSE cache (cache_duration_s=3600) causes silent file corruption when Edit/Write tools and bash interact
source_issues.evidence: cache_duration_s=3600 confirmed from server-side rclone mount config. Reproducible: write file with Edit tool, edit it, read it in bash — shows old content for up to 1 hour. Single project documented 8 files corrupted. Estimated 3-4 hours wasted per session. No error or warning raised. The uploads mount proves cache_duration_s=1 works for the same infrastructure.

signals.topic: Telegram MCP plugin silently stops receiving inbound messages (polling stalls permanently)
signals.summary: The Telegram plugin can silently halt its inbound polling while keeping the MCP server alive. Observed 7 times in 10 days. bot.start() can resolve without actual shutdown, causing the polling-retry loop to exit prematurely. Users receive no messages without any error logged. Also manifests as sibling session SIGTERM race and MCP disconnect after harness recycle.
signals.review_reason: Three independent reports covering three facets of the same Telegram plugin lifecycle failure: silent polling stall (issue 1673, 7 occurrences), SIGTERM race between sibling sessions (issue 1691), and MCP disconnect after harness recycle (issue 1680). All result in the same user experience: inbound Telegram messages stop arriving with no recovery. The silent polling stall is particularly dangerous as it produces no error and outbound calls still appear functional.

source_issues.title: fix(telegram): retry polling on silent bot.start() resolution
source_issues.evidence: bot.start() can resolve without shutdown signal, causing polling loop to exit prematurely. Observed 7 times in 10 days. Outbound API calls still work while inbound polling is dead. No error is logged. Only full process restart restores function.

source_issues.title: SIGTERM-on-startup race kills sibling Claude sessions sharing the same bot token
source_issues.evidence: server.ts sends SIGTERM to any PID found in bot.pid on startup, killing sibling Claude sessions that share the same Telegram bot token. The MCP plugin then disconnects. Standard multi-session setup (parent listener + child sessions for each message) is affected.

source_issues.title: [telegram] MCP disconnects mid-session and does not auto-reconnect after /mcp dialog or other plugin re-auth
source_issues.evidence: Opening /mcp dialog or any other MCP re-auth causes the Telegram MCP to disconnect. No auto-reconnect. User must run /reload-plugins manually. Observed multiple times in same session. Disruptive for long-running Telegram conversations.

signals.topic: iMessage: cross-device and phone-number self-chat failures cause silent message drops / reply blocks
signals.summary: Two related bugs prevent iMessage from functioning for self-chats: (1) Phone-number-based self-chats fail with AppleScript -1728 error on every reply attempt, leaving users with no response. (2) Cross-device self-chat messages (iPhone to Mac) are silently dropped because the plugin only checks is_from_me=1 rows for sent-receipts, missing the received content.
signals.review_reason: Two related bugs covering the entire self-chat message flow. Issue 1678 causes reply tool to fail on every phone-number self-chat with an uncaught AppleScript error. Issue 1676 causes inbound messages to be silently dropped for cross-device self-chats. Both result in zero agent response on a common use case (self-chat by phone number or multi-device Apple ID). The 'agent appears broken' perception is confirmed in issue 1678's severity note.

source_issues.title: imessage: reply tool fails with AppleScript -1728 for phone-number self-chats
source_issues.evidence: Reply tool returns AppleScript error -1728 for phone-number-based self-chats. Every reply attempt fails silently (error only in MCP logs). User sees no response from the agent. Root cause: Messages.app chat id lookup fails for phone-number GUIDs even when chat exists. Working patch provided.

source_issues.title: iMessage: cross-device self-chat messages silently dropped (is_from_me=1 only)
source_issues.evidence: handleInbound() returns early on is_from_me=1, which is correct for same-device sent receipts but incorrect for cross-device receives (iPhone→Mac). Messages from other devices arrive only as is_from_me=1 rows with content in attributedBody, and are silently dropped. No error logged, no reply sent. Self-chat entirely broken for multi-device setups.

signals.topic: Claude Code plugins are non-functional on Windows due to multiple path/shell incompatibilities
signals.summary: Multiple plugins fail on Windows due to Unix-specific paths and APIs: (1) typescript-lsp: libuv can't find typescript-language-server because .cmd shim is not resolved without shell:true. (2) SessionStart hook fails because /usr/bin/bash points to a PE executable on Windows. These make entire plugins dead on arrival for Windows users.
signals.review_reason: Two distinct Windows path/shell failures affecting core plugin functionality. Issue 1693 makes the TypeScript LSP plugin unusable on Windows (ENOENT on every startup). Issue 1692 makes SessionStart hooks fail on every Claude Code startup on Windows. Both are blocking failures for the Windows user segment (~30% of developers per issue 1665's own estimate).

source_issues.title: typescript-lsp: ENOENT on Windows — libuv can't spawn typescript-language-server (.cmd shim, no .exe)
source_issues.evidence: uv_spawn on Windows only resolves executables via PATHEXT if shell:true or explicit .cmd extension. The plugin hardcodes command without extension, causing ENOENT on every Windows install. TypeScript LSP plugin is completely non-functional on Windows.

source_issues.title: SessionStart hook fails on Windows: /usr/bin/bash is PE executable, not shell
source_issues.evidence: hooks/hooks.json hardcodes /usr/bin/bash which on Windows resolves to Git bash.exe (PE executable) that cannot interpret shell scripts. Error: 'cannot execute binary file'. SessionStart hook fails on every Claude Code startup on Windows. Reference to superpowers plugin's .cmd polyglot workaround provided.

signals.topic: iMessage chat_messages MCP tool gets stuck in infinite loop on HEIC image attachments causing agent hang
signals.summary: The iMessage MCP chat_messages tool auto-embeds image attachments inline. For iPhone-sourced HEIC photos (the default format since 2017), the Anthropic API returns HTTP 400 (HEIC not in supported format list). The tool retries or hangs indefinitely with no error surfaced to the agent, causing the agent to appear 'busy' indefinitely. Observed 12-minute stuck state requiring external restart.
aliases: iMessage HEIC image causes 400 loop and agent hang
iMessage HEIC exceeds 256KB Read tool limit
iMessage image attachment agent stuck state
signals.review_reason: Two related reports covering the same HEIC image failure path. Issue 1662 documents a 12-minute agent stuck state caused by the 400-and-loop behavior, requiring external restart. Issue 1656 documents the separate 256KB Read tool limit failure for HEIC. Both affect every iPhone user sending images over iMessage to the plugin — a common real-world scenario.

source_issues.title: chat_messages should support text-only mode (or fail-fast on attachment fetch) to bypass auto-embedded image fetches that 400-and-loop
source_issues.evidence: iPhone HEIC photos cause HTTP 400 from Anthropic API (HEIC not supported). Tool retries/hangs indefinitely with no error to agent. Agent appears 'busy' for 12 minutes until external restart. signals.topic: hookify: Write tool silently bypasses action:block security rules for file writes
signals.summary: The hookify plugin's event:file rules with action:block never fire when Claude uses the Write tool, because Write sends content via the 'content' key rather than 'new_string' that the rule engine checks. Security guardrails (credential detection, registry pinning, content policy) are silently ineffective for Write operations.
aliases: hookify Write tool bypasses block rules
event:file action:block ineffective for Write tool
signals.review_reason: Security enforcement is silently bypassed for the Write tool. Any user relying on hookify action:block rules for credential detection, registry pinning, or content policy is completely unprotected when Claude uses Write. This is a primary workflow security failure, not a minor edge case.

source_issues.title: hookify: Write tool silently bypasses event:file rules (action:block ineffective)
source_issues.evidence: Root cause identified: Write tool sends 'content' key but rule_engine.py only reads 'new_string' for 'event:file' rules, causing action:block to silently pass through. Reproduction test case provided. Security guardrails (credential detection, public registry blocking) provide zero enforcement for Write operations.

signals.topic: PDF skill: positional/auto-generated table extraction silently fails; pdftotext layout produces incorrect multi-page column alignment; memory leak causes OOM kill at ~3000 pages
signals.summary: Users extracting tables from auto-generated PDFs (Access exports, schema dumps, data dictionaries) encounter three compounding problems: (1) pdfplumber.extract_tables() returns empty results for positional tables lacking cell borders; (2) pdftotext -layout rescales column widths per-page based on widest line (header/footer), causing logical columns to land at different character positions on continuation pages, breaking layout-based parsers; (3) pdfplumber's per-page cache without explicit flush causes linear memory growth leading to OOM-kill at ~3000 pages on large documents. These issues are not documented in SKILL.md and users spend significant time on failed heuristics.
signals.review_reason: User impact is clear and multi-layered: (1) main workflow of extracting tables from a common PDF type (auto-generated, schema dumps) is completely broken silently; (2) the workaround pdftotext -layout produces subtly corrupted output on multi-page documents, which is non-obvious and breaks downstream parsing; (3) processing large PDFs causes OOM kills. Evidence from issue body is specific (3000-page threshold, 5500-page document, memory grows linearly). Count=1 but severity justifies P1; not P0 due to single-source.

source_issues.title: pdf skill: `pdftotext -layout` column-drift on multi-page positional "tables"
source_issues.evidence: extract_tables() returns nothing for positional tables; pdftotext rescales column widths per page causing continuation pages to have columns at wrong character positions; memory grows linearly without flush_cache(), OOM-killed at ~3000 pages on a 5500-page document; no documentation in SKILL.md; no fix available

While count=2, the primary source issue (1555) includes cross-reference to Issue #1434, providing corroborating evidence that this is a real, documented problem beyond a single report. The impact is a degraded automation experience with wasted inference cost and workflow interruptions, meeting the threshold for a P1 pain point.

signals.topic: MiniMax model subagent LLM calls consistently fail with HTTP 400 error code 2013

source_issues.title: MiniMax models return 400 'invalid chat setting (2013)' when subagent is invoked

signals.topic: ChatWithCrewFlow initialization makes blocking synchronous LLM calls at module import time, crashing containers on any LLM provider failure
signals.summary: ChatWithCrewFlow.__init__ invokes generate_crew_chat_inputs which makes synchronous LLM calls at Python module import time — before the web server binds to a port. Any LLM provider hiccup (500, 503, rate-limit, DNS failure, invalid credentials) causes the process to exit with code 1. Container orchestrators (Railway, Kubernetes, ECS, Fly.io) mark the deployment as failed and roll back, making the entire service unavailable.
aliases: container crash on LLM failure startup
signals.review_reason: This is a production deployment blocker: the entire service becomes unavailable on any transient LLM failure during startup. No workaround exists — the crash occurs at module import before the application is even listening. Clearly satisfies '主流程阻断' (main flow blocking) as the whole service fails to deploy.

source_issues.title: ChatWithCrewFlow.__init__ makes blocking LLM call at module import, crashes containers on any LLM hiccup
source_issues.evidence: ChatWithCrewFlow.__init__ calls generate_crew_chat_inputs() which makes synchronous blocking LLM calls at import time, BEFORE uvicorn/FastAPI binds to HTTP port. Any LLM failure causes Python process to exit with code 1, crashing the container. Container orchestrators mark deployment as failed and roll back. No workaround available.

signals.topic: Converter module makes synchronous LLM calls in async workflows (akickoff), blocking the event loop
signals.summary: When using akickoff() with Task(output_json=...) or Task(output_pydantic=...), the converter module makes synchronous self.llm.call() which blocks the event loop. This breaks the async nature of akickoff(), potentially causing hangs or deadlocks in async applications.
aliases: sync LLM call in async workflow
signals.review_reason: Blocking synchronous calls in an async event loop is a fundamental correctness violation. It causes async applications to hang or deadlock, blocking the main async workflow. The user cannot complete async tasks that also use structured output format.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Do not invoke synchronous call() on LLM from asynchronous workflow in _export_output / converter
source_issues.evidence: In an async workflow via akickoff(), the converter module makes synchronous self.llm.call() which blocks the event loop. This violates asyncio contract and can cause deadlocks/hangs. Specifically affects tasks using output_json or output_pydantic in async workflows. No workaround — sync and async calls cannot be mixed safely.

signals.topic: InternalInstructor silently discards base_url when creating instructor client, breaking all OpenAI-compatible self-hosted LLM structured output
signals.summary: When using output_pydantic or output_json with a self-hosted LLM (vLLM, Ollama, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint with a custom base_url), InternalInstructor._create_instructor_client() extracts only model name and provider, then calls instructor.from_provider() which defaults to api.openai.com. The base_url is silently discarded, causing ConnectTimeout errors for environments that cannot reach OpenAI.
signals.review_reason: Critical feature breakage for self-hosted LLM users: the structured output feature (output_pydantic/output_json) is completely non-functional because all requests silently redirect to api.openai.com. This makes a key feature unusable for an entire class of users (self-hosted deployments).

source_issues.title: [BUG] InternalInstructor discards base_url when creating instructor client — breaks OpenAI-compatible endpoints
source_issues.evidence: InternalInstructor._create_instructor_client() extracts only model name and provider, calls instructor.from_provider() which defaults to api.openai.com/v1/. The base_url from the LLM object is never forwarded. Users running self-hosted vLLM/Ollama cannot use output_pydantic or output_json — structured output feature is completely broken for them. Results in ConnectTimeout errors to api.openai.com.

signals.topic: ConditionalTask with output_pydantic and guardrail causes TypeError: json.loads receives PydanticModel instead of string
signals.summary: When using ConditionalTask with output_pydantic, a custom guardrail, and context from another task that also uses output_pydantic, CrewAI internally calls json.loads() on a Pydantic object instead of its serialized JSON string. This causes TypeError: 'the JSON object must be str, bytes or bytearray, not <PydanticModel>'. The crew execution fails completely.
signals.review_reason: This is a specific feature combination failure (ConditionalTask + output_pydantic + guardrail + cross-task context) that causes complete workflow failure with no workaround. While count=1, the evidence clearly shows crew execution failure with a TypeError, satisfying the '主流程阻断' criterion for a real user pain point.

source_issues.title: [BUG] TypeError: the JSON object must be str, bytes or bytearray, not <PydanticModel> when combining ConditionalTask + output_pydantic + guardrail + context
source_issues.evidence: CrewAI calls json.loads() on a Pydantic object (DrugClassificationOutput) instead of calling .model_dump_json() first. Occurs specifically when ConditionalTask references a context task with output_pydantic AND also has its own output_pydantic and guardrail. 'Crew Execution Failed' with no workaround. The feature combination is fundamentally broken.

signals.topic: Converter JSON regex pattern produces false positives on GraphQL schemas and curly-brace content, breaking output_pydantic
signals.summary: The converter module uses a regex pattern _JSON_PATTERN = re.compile(r'({.*})', re.DOTALL) to detect JSON in agent output. This pattern falsely matches any curly-brace content including GraphQL schemas, causing Pydantic validation to fail with 'Invalid JSON: key must be a string'. Tasks using output_pydantic fail when agents return structured content that resembles but is not valid JSON.
aliases: GraphQL schema false positive JSON detection
output_pydantic fails on curly brace content
signals.review_reason: The regex-based JSON detection produces clear false positives causing Pydantic validation errors. This breaks the output_pydantic feature for any agent output containing curly-brace text that isn't valid JSON (GraphQL schemas being the explicit example). User workflow is blocked when this feature is used with structured text.

source_issues.title: [BUG] when using Task(..., output_pydantic=MyModel) some JSON substring identification within the data occurs with possible false positive
source_issues.evidence: The regex pattern ({.*}) with DOTALL matches multi-line GraphQL schemas (e.g., 'type Query { countries: [Country] }') as JSON, then Pydantic validation fails with 'key must be a string'. Any agent output containing curly-brace text that isn't valid JSON (GraphQL, template strings, etc.) causes output_pydantic tasks to fail.

signals.topic: Groq API rejects requests when pattern input becomes only a system message (last role must be 'user')
signals.summary: Fabric constructs chat payloads with only a system message when patterns place INPUT in system.md, but Groq's chat.completions API requires the last message role to be 'user'. This causes 400 errors that block built-in patterns like summarize when using the Groq vendor.
aliases: Groq vendor chat.completions role validation failure
system-only message payload rejected by Groq
signals.review_reason: This is a clear main-flow blocking bug: users who configure the Groq vendor cannot use built-in patterns because the API rejects the constructed payload. The error is reproducible (400 from Groq API) and affects a core workflow (pattern execution). Not P0 because count=1 and only affects Groq vendor users.

Not P0 because count=1, but review_reason provides clear user impact evidence (API call entirely blocked).

signals.topic: BaseSandbox.ls silently swallows FileNotFoundError and PermissionError, returning indistinguishable empty result
signals.summary: When calling ls on a non-existent path or a path without read permission, BaseSandbox.ls catches the exception silently and returns LsResult(entries=[]) — identical to a legitimately empty directory. Users cannot detect file access errors and workflows proceed with incorrect assumptions.

signals.topic: SubAgentMiddleware IndexError crash when subagent returns empty messages list
signals.summary: SubAgentMiddleware._return_command_with_state_update validates the 'messages' key exists but does not check if the list is non-empty before accessing result['messages'][-1]. When a subagent completes with an empty messages list, the function crashes with IndexError: list index out of range, terminating the parent workflow.
signals.review_reason: 未处理的 IndexError 导致父工作流直接崩溃，是明确的主流程崩溃。只要子 Agent 返回空消息列表就会触发，必然阻断使用子 Agent 功能的用户。两个 Issue 从不同用户视角报告了同一问题，证实了用户影响。

signals.topic: BaseSandbox.read() returns base64-encoded content instead of text for valid UTF-8 files when multi-byte characters span the 8192-byte sniff boundary
signals.summary: BaseSandbox.read() uses an 8192-byte prefix to detect encoding. When a multi-byte UTF-8 character is split at the 8192-byte boundary, the sniff logic incorrectly detects binary content and returns base64 instead of text. Users receive corrupted/unusable file content with no indication it is encoded.
aliases: BaseSandbox read returns base64 instead of text UTF-8 boundary
file read binary detection false positive
signals.review_reason: 文件读取是 Agent 最基础的操作之一。当文件内容被静默转换为 base64 而非文本，用户收到的是乱码/不可用内容。这对需要处理包含多字节字符文件的用户造成主流程失败（文件内容不可用），但触发条件较特殊（需在 8192 字节边界恰好截断多字节字符）。

source_issues.title: BaseSandbox.read() returns base64 for valid UTF-8 files when multi-byte char straddles 8192-byte sniff boundary

signals.topic: CompositeBackend virtual paths not resolved in LocalShellBackend.execute, causing agent retry loops
signals.summary: When a skill references a virtual path like python /common/skills/yyy/xxx.py, CompositeBackend routes read/ls/grep by path prefix, but execute always delegates to the default backend which sees a literal OS path. The command fails and the agent enters a retry loop probing with ls/grep, reinforcing the wrong mental model.
aliases: execute command fails with virtual filesystem paths
signals.review_reason: 虚拟路径是 CompositeBackend 的核心路由机制，当技能使用虚拟路径执行命令时主流程直接失败并陷入重试循环，直接阻断 Agent 核心功能（通过技能执行命令）。用户可见的重复失败行为浪费时间和 token。

signals.topic: deepagents-cli hides server-side traceback when langgraph_api strips error message, making debugging nearly impossible
signals.summary: Any condition that makes the langgraph dev server raise an exception whose type is outside langgraph_api/serde.py's serialization whitelist causes the entire error message to be dropped. The CLI receives an empty error response and shows no useful information to the user, making diagnosis of real failures extremely difficult.
aliases: CLI hides traceback on non-serializable errors
error message stripped by langgraph_api serde
signals.review_reason: 用户遇到真实错误时完全看不到任何错误信息，导致无法诊断和解决实际问题。这不是崩溃但严重损害用户体验，属于关键调试功能不可用，对需要排查生产问题的用户影响显著。

signals.topic: HumanInTheLoopMiddleware executes rejected tool calls in LangGraph's ToolNode
signals.summary: When a human reviewer explicitly rejects a tool call via decision[type] == reject, the middleware returns the tool_call with a tool_message, but the rejected tool_call is never removed from AIMessage.tool_calls. LangGraph's ToolNode then blindly executes the rejected tool, ignoring the user's rejection intent — a core safety mechanism failure.
signals.review_reason: This is a main flow failure. HumanInTheLoopMiddleware is a core safety mechanism designed to let humans review and reject tool calls before execution. When a human explicitly rejects a tool call, the tool still runs — directly contradicting user intent and bypassing the safety check entirely. This is blocking for any production use of HITL where human oversight is critical (e.g., financial transactions, data deletion, external API calls).

source_issues.title: HumanInTheLoopMiddleware executes rejected tool calls in LangGraph's ToolNode
source_issues.evidence: When a human reviewer rejects a tool call via decision[type] == reject, the middleware returns (tool_call, tool_message). The rejected tool_call is not removed from AIMessage.tool_calls, so LangGraph's ToolNode blindly executes it. The user's rejection intent is completely ignored — main flow failure and core safety mechanism bypass.

signals.topic: merge_dicts concatenates ls_provider across streaming chunks, inflating response_metadata
signals.summary: merge_dicts() concatenates ls_provider string values across streaming chunks. After ~20 chunks, ls_provider grows from 'amazon_bedrock' (14 chars) to 280+ chars. Every AIMessage carries this inflated metadata, causing payload bloat in production LangGraph agent conversations.
signals.review_reason: This causes significant UX degradation through payload bloat in production. In LangGraph agents with many steps, every AIMessage accumulates inflated metadata, causing request payload growth. This leads to increased latency, potential API throttling from larger payloads, and degraded performance. The bug is repeatable across all streaming responses using ChatBedrockConverse and similar providers that set ls_provider per chunk.

source_issues.title: Bug: merge_dicts concatenates ls_provider across streaming chunks, inflating response_metadata
source_issues.evidence: merge_dicts() concatenates ls_provider string values across chunks. Production impact: payload bloat in LangGraph agent conversations with 58+ graph steps, leading to increased latency and potential API throttling.

signals.topic: PostgresStore numeric filter operators ($gt, $gte, $lt, $lte) silently return wrong query results due to lexicographic text comparison

Users filtering by numeric ranges get incorrect results (items with score=2-9 pass a {"$gte": 10} filter). This is a main flow failure in a core data operation (kv store lookups), with evidence of actual incorrect behavior demonstrated in the issue.

signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking: langgraph dev cannot restart immediately after Ctrl+C due to TCP TIME-WAIT holding the port. Forces users to wait ~60 seconds or use a different port. This is a significant development workflow disruption that interrupts the primary dev loop.

signals.topic: BinaryOperatorAggregate.update silently drops values arriving after Overwrite in concurrent supersteps
signals.summary: ch.update([Overwrite(10), 5]) expected: 15, actual: 10 — the 5 is silently dropped. In concurrent supersteps, task write ordering within apply_writes determines which values survive, causing non-deterministic data loss.
signals.review_reason: Main flow data integrity failure: BinaryOperatorAggregate silently discards values in concurrent scenarios. When Overwrite and regular values arrive in the same batch, the regular value is dropped without error. This causes non-deterministic state loss that is extremely hard to debug.
